Messages.Author: Ankur Gupta
Messages.Body:
I'd just like a clarification on the text of Maabara.

Maabara
Type: Master
Requires: Harbinger of Skulls
Master: unique location.
You may tap this location to move a card from your ash heap to this
location. You may use a master phase action to move a card from this
location to the top of your library. Any vampire may burn this location as
a (D) action.

I'd just like to make sure that the "card moved from the ash heap" can't
be a vampire card. It doesn't specify, but I'd figure that it's important
to clarify this, since it causes all kinds of problems if you have a
vampire in your hand. :)

Ankur Gupta
Prince of West Lafayette

Messages.Author: Fabio 'Sooner' Macedo
Messages.Body:


In that thread, LSJ states that library cards cannot be in the crypt
and vice-versa.

But I wonder... What if I want to put a crypt card on Maabara just to
avoid some (admittedly cornercase) situations such as:
- my predator controls Yong Sun (whichever version has the +bleed bonus
for vampires in its prey's ash heap)
- someone is playing Necromancy and I know he/she has a Daemonic
Possession at hand (and my vampire was burned since last turn blah
blah)
- someone has a Vulture's Buffet, Lifeless Tongues, Emergency Rations
or whatever card that takes advantage of a burned minion and I don't
want the player to target my vampire with it for whatever reason

Maabara's card text allows me to put the crypt card in it, right. But
some examples in the thread above mentioned things like Banishing an
Embrace card and then playing, say, Kaymakli Nightmares to return
vampires in the uncontrolled region to the crypt. LSJ said it just
makes the Embrace card go to the ash heap instead. Doesn't it suggest
that I *could* try to move the the crypt card on Maabara to the top of
the library, but it just goes to the ash heap instead?

Not much of an issue since one can stack as many cards on Maabara as he
wants, but just want to be sure that effects that make cards go to a
place where they do not belong can be played/called upon or not. Maybe
I want to use Maabara to protect a vampire from the cornercase
situations above, and once the potential threats to that vampire's
"well being" are out of the game, I could want the crypt card back to
the ash heap to play Possession, or whatever. Is it possible at all?

Fabio "Sooner" Macedo
